links.outcome: Measurement-confirmed failures among AI/complexity-flagged radiotherapy plans
links.effect: Measurement-based PSQA confirmed 9 out of 29 flagged plans as actual failures; these were re-optimized until no longer ranked at risk.
links.quote: After the PSQA measurements, 9 out of 29 plans were found to be actual failures and were re-optimized such that they were no longer ranked at risk.

links.outcome: Predicted gamma passing rate before and after workflow-triggered corrective actions
links.effect: Median expected GPR increased from 97.4 % [92.0, 98.8]% to 98.2 % [96.2, 99.1]% after corrective actions (p = 0.007); this was a predicted, not measured, outcome.
links.quote: With corrective actions, the distribution of the expected GPR significantly improved (p = 0.007), with an increase in the median – [first, third] quartile – from 97.4 % [92.0, 98.8]% to 98.2 % [96.2, 99.1]%, as shown in Fig. 3 .

links.effect: A preliminary phase revealed potential non-utilization of the tool when accessed manually, prompting the implementation of an automated daily email to alert planners of at-risk cases.
links.quote: In a preliminary phase, the DSS tool could be used only within the TPS. Then, a Poka Yoke approach was implemented to sustain the solution and address the potential miss of plans at risk of PSQA failure due to the non-utilization of the tool.

unlisted_practices: Using automated background AI screening and push notifications (such as emails) for high-risk cases rather than relying on clinicians to manually initiate an optional AI tool
